sources.title: A History of Modern Yemen
sources.note: Cambridge historical synthesis on Qasimid rule, regional diversity, collapse, famine, disease, and Ottoman return.

sources.title: Tribes, Government, and History in Yemen
sources.note: Oxford monograph integrating local histories, documents, fieldwork, tribal organization, livelihood, learning, and government.

sources.title: History from the Qasimis to the Hamid al-Din
sources.note: Oxford chapter tracing seventeenth-century expansion, nineteenth-century disasters, state collapse, and later Ottoman occupation.

sources.title: Revival and Reform in Islam: The Legacy of Muhammad al-Shawkani
sources.note: Cambridge study of Qasimid political change, scholarship, Sunni traditionism, and Muhammad al-Shawkani.

sources.title: Zaydism at the Crossroads
sources.note: Cambridge chapter dating Qasimid collapse to 1853, subsequent disorder, Ottoman rule, and later Zaydi continuity.

sources.title: From Paris to Taif: Sovereignty, Borders, and Minorities in Arabia
sources.note: Peer-reviewed chronology of Qasimid Yemen, coffee revenue, nineteenth-century intervention, Aden, and Ottoman occupation.

sources.title: The Ottoman Empire and the Indian Ocean
sources.note: Oxford account of revolts beginning in 1597, Ottoman abandonment, Indian Ocean strategy, and nineteenth-century return.

sources.title: Yemen's Manuscript Culture
sources.note: Library of Congress hosted scholarly chapter on Qasimid expansion, Ottoman withdrawal, coffee prosperity, and manuscript renewal.

sources.title: Coffee in the Red Sea Area from the Sixteenth to the Nineteenth Century
sources.note: Cambridge economic history of terrace cultivation, marketing networks, ports, consumption, and global competition.

sources.title: The Merchant Houses of Mocha
sources.note: University of Washington Press study of merchants, architecture, social hierarchy, households, and Indian Ocean connections.

sources.title: Shipped but Not Sold
sources.note: University of Hawaii Press study of everyday cargo, gifts, ceremonies, coffee service, textiles, medicines, and trade tools.

sources.title: Lost in Translation: the Anglo-Yemeni Treaty of 1821
sources.note: Peer-reviewed study of Qasimid diplomacy, Mocha communities, translation, subjecthood, and al-Shawkani as chief judge.

sources.title: Waqf in Zaydi Yemen
sources.note: Brill monograph on Qasimid Zaydism, charitable endowments, courts, Lower Yemen, and learned institutions.

sources.title: Dissembling Descent, or How the Barber Lost His Turban
sources.note: Peer-reviewed case study of identity, evidence, hierarchy, and justice in eighteenth-century Zaydi Yemen.

sources.title: The Mawza Exile at the Juncture of Zaydi and Ottoman Messianism
sources.note: Peer-reviewed history of Yemeni Jewish life, restrictions, persecution, and the Qasimid-era Mawza exile.

sources.title: The Forced Conversion of Jewish Orphans in Yemen
sources.note: Peer-reviewed analysis of an eighteenth-century Zaydi legal interpretation and its effects on orphaned Jewish children.

sources.title: Yemeni Manuscript Digitization Initiative
sources.note: University-led preservation program documenting Yemen's extensive private Arabic manuscript libraries and partner institutions.

sources.title: Nayl al-awtar min ahadith Sayyid al-Akhyar
sources.note: Library catalog record securing the Arabic title, author, transliteration, and language of al-Shawkani's work.

sources.title: Kitab Unmudhaj fi al-tibb
sources.note: Princeton catalog for a seventeenth-century Arabic medical manuscript from the al-Madani library collection.

sources.title: al-Insan fi al-tibb
sources.note: Library of Congress catalog for a late eighteenth-century Arabic treatise on health, nutrition, medication, and disease.

sources.title: Old City of Sanaa
sources.note: UNESCO account of tower houses, materials, gardens, mosques, hammams, and the historic urban fabric.

sources.title: Bayt al-Belayli
sources.note: Archnet record for a seventeenth-century Sanaa tower house and its family, storage, reception, and social spaces.

sources.title: Historic Town of Zabid
sources.note: UNESCO account of canals, mosques, madrasas, courtyard houses, privacy, markets, and international learning.

sources.title: UNESCO Expert Mission to Zabid
sources.note: UNESCO technical study describing traditional materials, courtyards, wells, latrines, washing places, kitchens, and ventilation.

sources.title: Farming Systems and Poverty: Highland Mixed Farming
sources.note: FAO synthesis of Yemeni terraces, cereals, legumes, coffee, qat, fruit, livestock, water rights, and household farming.

sources.title: Necklace, Yemen, nineteenth century
sources.note: Metropolitan Museum object record linking Jewish silversmiths, coffee currency, Indian forms, and bridal trousseaux.

sources.title: Yemeni legal document dated 1764
sources.note: Princeton Geniza catalog for a Yemen legal document in Arabic and Judaeo-Arabic with six witness clauses.

sources.title: A Short Chronology of Yemen
sources.note: Oxford chronology dating British capture of Aden and the Ottoman conquest of Sanaa in 1872.

sources.title: Between Commerce and Sanctity in the Early Modern Red Sea
sources.note: Peer-reviewed account of Ottoman withdrawal, coffee expansion, Mocha, European companies, and Red Sea commerce.

proposedOverrides.name: Qasimid Imamate of Yemen
proposedOverrides.summary: The Qasimid imams expelled Ottoman forces, ruled much of western Yemen through a coffee-rich but negotiated state, and collapsed amid fragmentation in 1853.
